object.dateLabel: c. 450–500 CE (text); this copy 19th century or earlier
object.medium: Ink-rubbed incised script on dried palm leaf
object.description: A single leaf of a palm-leaf manuscript of the Tirukkural (திருக்குறள்), the most loved book in the Tamil language. The Kural is a collection of 1,330 couplets, each of just seven words, on virtue, wealth and love, written by the poet Valluvar (திருவள்ளுவர்) around the fifth century CE, perhaps earlier. This leaf carries the first two couplets, beginning 'As the letter A is the first of all letters, so the primal God is first in the world', with the commentary of the thirteenth-century scholar Parimelalhagar written between the lines of verse. For over a thousand years the text survived only this way: letters scratched with a stylus into strips of dried palmyra leaf, the grooves rubbed with soot or lamp-black, the leaves strung together and recopied every century or two before they crumbled. The Kural was the first book printed in Tamil, in 1812, from blocks cut to imitate leaves like this one. It is quoted in Tamil homes, courts and parliaments to this day.
facts: 1,330 couplets in 133 chapters of ten; every couplet has exactly seven words in the kural metre.
Nothing certain is known about the author; the honorific Thiruvalluvar means 'the revered Valluvar'.
Dated by linguists to about 450–500 CE; traditional accounts place it earlier, in the Sangam age.
Translated into more than forty languages; the first English selection appeared in 1794.
